neighbor_relevance.note: Real BGer corpus. Citation pairs as weak supervision. TF-IDF strongly separates citing decisions (AUC > 0.95). Full TF-IDF slightly outperforms reasoning-only, suggesting shared boilerplate helps citation matching.

boilerplate_resistance.note: Real BGer corpus. TF-IDF is catastrophically sensitive to boilerplate (0.01 resistance). Adding ~100 words of standard BGer procedural text changes embedding by 99%. Legal representations must achieve >0.5.

multilingual_invariance.note: Real BGer corpus. TF-IDF is completely language-specific. Cross-language same-branch pairs have near-zero similarity (0.03). Negative separation means language dominates over legal content.

corpus_stability.note: Real BGer corpus. TF-IDF retrained on growing subsets has very high drift (0.87). Vocabulary shift with new documents dramatically repositions existing decisions.

hierarchy_coherence.note: Real BGer corpus. Moderate purity (0.47-0.65) but near-zero NMI (0.01-0.03). Clusters capture some legal structure but primarily separate by language, not legal area.
